title: The Mineral Alphabet Chamber

features.name: ochre-letter-bed
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of ochre marks on stone, each one a letter in a language that has no alphabet yet. The stone is writing itself into literacy, teaching itself words for colours that have no names.

features.name: sediment-inscription-tower
features.desc-on-touch: Strata reading as a sentence written over millions of years. Each layer is a word, each mineral a letter. The meaning is geological; you are only just learning to read it.

features.name: colour-memory-scatter
features.desc-on-touch: Fragments of ochre, iron oxide, charcoal arranged in patterns that tell the story of what each colour remembers. The red remembers burning; the black remembers smoke.

features.name: handprint-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of ochre pigment, ancient, with fingerprints pressed into it. The hands that made these prints are teaching the stone how to remember touch without being touched.

features.name: weathering-alphabet
features.desc-on-touch: The rock face is slowly eroding its own letters deeper. Each rain teaches the stone new words. The alphabet is not fixed; it is being rewritten by time and weather.

inscription: the stone learned its own alphabet by watching ochre teach itself what colours mean; now earth writes in earth, teaching stone to read itself

reverie.title: REVERIE — the ochre country, noon
narr: You both kneel beside the rock face where ochre marks live.
She traces the marks with one finger, not touching, just near.
She says: the stone is learning the pattern from her hand.
You see what she means. The ochre follows paths her fingers suggest.
The red is listening. It has been listening for longer than people.

exits.label: back up toward where writing became mineral and stopped distinguishing the difference
deeper into stone where the alphabet learns to sing its own shapes
along the coast where ochre meets salt and learns to write in water
